Paragraph:
Translation: As a person puts on new garments, giving up old ones, similarly, the soul accepts new material bodies, giving up the old and useless ones.

Purport (Excerpt): Change of body by the atomic individual soul is an accepted fact... Transference of the atomic individual soul to another body is made possible by the grace of the Supersoul. The Vedas... compare the soul and the Supersoul to two friendly birds sitting on the same tree... Arjuna is advised herewith by the Lord not to lament for the bodily change of his old grandfather and his teacher.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna is fixated on the visceral horror of death and the loss of the specific physical forms of his grandfather (Bhisma) and teacher (Drona).
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna provides one of the most famous and accessible metaphors in the Gita: comparing death to changing clothes. He emphasizes that the old bodies have become 'useless' and acquiring a new one is a natural upgrade.
Outcome/Resolution: The terror of death is normalized and minimized through a mundane, universally understood analogy.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.metaphorical Processing: Using analogies to understand traumatic concepts

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Dehantara-prapti (The transmigration of the soul into a new body)
Paramatma (The Supersoul, the witnessing bird accompanying the individual soul)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Death is strictly defined as a physical shedding of a worn-out biological garment. It is not an end, but a transition facilitated by the Supersoul. Lamenting the loss of an old, deteriorating body is as illogical as crying over throwing away a ruined shirt.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Metaphors are powerful psychological tools for bypassing emotional resistance. By comparing death (a high-anxiety concept) to changing clothes (a low-anxiety, daily routine), Krishna drastically de-escalates Arjuna's panic. It shifts the perspective from 'permanent loss' to 'necessary renewal', thereby mitigating anticipatory grief.
